db.query.summary: Runs a read SQL query and returns all the rows.
db.query.details: Each row is a table { column = value }. Tables and columns are named as in the grid; a name with a space, an accent or a capital letter goes in double quotes ("Amount excl. tax"). Each table has a hidden column _id, the key of the row. The ? take the following parameters (number, text, boolean or nil). At most 100,000 rows: beyond that, use db.rows. An empty cell gives nil (the key is missing from the row), a boolean true/false, a date a text "yyyy-mm-dd".

db.rows.signature: for row in db.rows(sql, ...) do ... end
db.rows.summary: Goes through the rows of a query one by one, with no limit on their number.
db.rows.details: Same rules as db.query, but the rows are not all kept in memory: better for large tables.

db.value.summary: Returns the first column of the first row, or nil if there is no row.

db.tables.summary: Lists the tables of the workbook with their columns.
db.tables.details: Each column is { name, type, fixed }; type is "integer", "decimal", "text", "boolean" or "date", fixed is true if the type was set by hand.

db.insert.summary: Adds a row at the end of a table and returns its key _id.
db.insert.details: Values are handled like typing in the grid: a column with an inferred type widens, a column with a fixed type marks the entry as invalid, "" leaves the cell empty. true and false are written as vrai and faux (TRUE and FALSE); a date is given as text ("16/10/2026"). Table and column names must be exact (capitals and accents included).

db.update.summary: Changes the given columns of row _id; the others do not move.
db.update.details: Same writing rules as db.insert. "" clears the cell.

db.delete.summary: Deletes row _id; the table shrinks by one row.

db.execute.summary: Runs an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE with the displayed names.
db.execute.details: Undoable like the rest of the script. Columns are strictly typed: a value of the wrong type makes the whole query fail (a boolean is written 1 or 0, a date 'yyyy-mm-dd'). Refused for now: CREATE, ALTER, DROP and the internal tables _lattis_*.

print.summary: Shows values in the output, separated by a tab.

type.summary: Returns the type of a value, as text.

tonumber.summary: Converts a text to a number; returns nil if it is not a number.
tonumber.details: The decimal separator is the dot: tonumber("80,5") gives nil.

ipairs.signature: for i, v in ipairs(list) do ... end
ipairs.summary: Goes through a list in order (indexes 1, 2, 3...) up to the first gap.

pairs.signature: for key, v in pairs(t) do ... end
pairs.summary: Goes through all the keys of a table, in no guaranteed order.

next.summary: Returns the next key of a table; next(t) == nil tests whether it is empty.

select.summary: Returns the arguments from the n-th on, or their number with "#".

unpack.summary: Returns the items of a list as separate values.

pcall.summary: Calls f and catches its error; ok is false on error.

xpcall.summary: Like pcall, but passes the error message to a handling function.

error.summary: Stops the script (or the running pcall) with a message.

assert.summary: Stops the script with the message if the condition is false (nil or false).

setmetatable.summary: Attaches a metatable to a table (default values, operators...).

getmetatable.summary: Returns the metatable of a value.

rawget.summary: Reads a key without going through the metatable.

rawset.summary: Writes a key without going through the metatable.

rawequal.summary: Compares two values without going through the metatable.

string.format.summary: Formats values: %s text, %d integer, %.2f decimal, %5s width, %% the % sign.

string.sub.summary: Extracts the characters from i to j (indexes from 1, negative ones from the end).
string.sub.details: Indexes count bytes: an accented letter takes two.

string.find.signature: s:find(pattern [, start [, plain]]) → start, end or nil
string.find.summary: Searches for a pattern; plain = true searches for the text as is.
string.find.details: Patterns: %d digit, %a letter, %s space, %w alphanumeric, . any character, * + - ? repetitions, ^ $ anchors, % to escape. These are not regular expressions.

string.match.summary: Returns what matches the pattern, or its captures in parentheses.

string.gmatch.signature: for m in s:gmatch(pattern) do ... end
string.gmatch.summary: Goes through all the matches of a pattern.

string.gsub.summary: Replaces the matches; the replacement can be a text, a table or a function.

string.rep.summary: Repeats a text n times (result limited to 16 MB).

string.byte.summary: Returns the codes of the bytes from i to j.

string.char.summary: Builds a text from byte codes.

table.insert.summary: Adds a value at the end of a list, or at the given position.

table.remove.summary: Removes the last item, or the one at the given position.

table.sort.summary: Sorts a list in place; before(a, b) returns true if a must come before b.

table.concat.summary: Joins the items of a list into one text.

table.maxn.summary: Returns the largest numeric index of a table.

math.floor.summary: Rounds down to an integer; math.floor(a / b) does an integer division.

math.fmod.summary: Remainder of the division (sign of x); see also the % operator.

math.modf.summary: Splits the integer part and the decimal part.

math.random.summary: Random number: real in [0, 1[, integer in [1, m] or [m, n].

math.pi.summary: The number π (a value, not a function).

math.atan2.summary: Arctangent of y/x, in the right quadrant.

os.date.summary: Formats a date: %d day, %m month, %Y year, %H:%M:%S time.
os.date.details: Workbook dates are in the format "yyyy-mm-dd", that is os.date("%Y-%m-%d"); they then compare like texts.

os.time.signature: os.time([{year, month, day, hour, min, sec}]) → seconds
os.time.summary: Returns the current time, or that of the given date, in seconds.

os.difftime.summary: Difference between two times returned by os.time.

os.clock.summary: Processor time used: measures how long a task takes.

local.summary: Declares a local variable. Without local, the variable is global.
local.details: A name contains only unaccented letters, digits and _. Only nil and false are false: 0 and "" are true.

if.summary: Condition. Not equal is written ~=; and, or and not are the logical operators.

for.signature: for i = start, stop [, step] do ... end
for.summary: Numeric loop; for ... in is for iterators (ipairs, pairs, db.rows).
for.details: break leaves the loop; there is no continue.

for in.signature: for i, v in ipairs(list) do ... end  |  for k, v in pairs(t) do ... end
for in.summary: Goes through a list in order (ipairs) or all the keys of a table (pairs, any order).

while.summary: Conditional loops. An endless loop is stopped after 30 s or by the Stop button.

function.signature: local function name(a, b) ... return x end
function.summary: Defines a function; it can return several values.

table.summary: The only data structure: list (indexes from 1) or dictionary.
table.details: #t gives the length of a list. A key with an accent or a space is written t["Payé"].

...summary: Concatenates two texts (or numbers). # gives the length, [[ ... ]] writes a text over several lines.

--.summary: Comment on one line, or over several lines.
